story: A powerful deity of war, iron, hunting, and metalworking was among the primordial deities who first came to Earth. Using a metal machete and aided by a dog, he cleared a path so that the other primordial deities could enter the world, earning him the epithet "first of the primordial deities to come to Earth." According to some legends, after the death of a ruler who had reigned twice, once before and once after another ruler, this deity attempted to seize the throne of an empire, but was ousted by a rival successor and sent into exile. In his earthly life, he became the first king of a city called Ire. He fought throughout his life on behalf of the people of that city, and was also known by a name meaning "of Ire." According to the stories, when some of his subjects failed to show him proper respect, he killed them, and then killed himself with his own sword. However, his followers do not believe he died; instead they say he "disappeared into the earth's surface." He vanished into the ground at a specific place called Ire-Ekiti, promising to help anyone who called upon his name. He continues to be venerated in several regions associated with his legend.
